_comment: FROZEN INPUT for the GLM7 integration-benchmark N=1 record. All fields are faithfully extracted from the paper's own full text (methods/results). Do not edit to match a desired outcome; edit only to correct a transcription error against the source, and re-stamp fulltext_sha256.
tier_rationale: Real paper, methods-text + declared-feature coverage (RAG + LLM + the disease-KB definition check on declared features). NOT full 33-gate execution: that consumes evidence/*.json from an instrumented training run, which a published paper does not emit (see integration-benchmark-PLAN.md S5).
title: GLM7 – A Novel Composite Glycolipid Index Derived from Routine Health Indicators for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prediction of Multimorbidity

source.in_peer_review_kb_note: Confirmed absent (DOI / 'glm7' / cohort size 26289 all not present). So this is a genuine OUT-OF-KB external paper: RAG retrieval cannot self-leak this paper's own concerns; LOPO exclusion is a declared no-op here.

design.declared_quote: A total of 26 289 individuals were included in this cross-sectional investigation, all of whom were participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted over the period of 2013-2023.
framing_quotes: Harnessing routine health examination data efficiently to predict the future onset of multiple diseases is critical
its significant potential as a novel diagnostic and predictive tool for diseases in the future
The outcome variables included the incidence of all diseases
design.framing_conflict: Data are explicitly cross-sectional (NHANES/CHARLS surveys with no follow-up; predictors and outcomes measured at the same visit), so all ascertained cases are PREVALENT; yet outcomes are labeled 'incidence' and the index is marketed for 'future onset' prediction.

external_cohort.name: CHARLS
external_cohort.note: Reported as 'external validation', but the text reports BOTH a training and a validation AUROC within CHARLS (model re-fit inside the external cohort) -> not a clean transportability test.

DM.definition_quote: DM was defined as having a history of diabetes or an HbA1c level > 6.5%.

CVD.definition_quote: CVD was defined as the presence of any of the following conditions: heart failure, stroke, coronary artery disease, heart attack (myocardial infarction), and angina pectoris, or as having a history of CVD.

liver_disease.definition_quote: diagnosed with any liver condition by a physician

cancer.definition_quote: diagnosed with any neoplastic disease by a physician

comorbidity.definition_quote: the presence of any of the following conditions: failing kidneys, chronic bronchitis, thyroid problems, and rheumatoid disorders.
comorbidity.note: 'failing kidneys' is the CKD/renal-failure component; predictors include BUN and Cr (creatinine), which are CKD definition variables.

predictors.glm7_formula: log10[Age * BMI * FBG * Insulin * TG * LDL-c / HDL-c]
predictors.glm7_formula_note: The composite predictor itself embeds FBG and Insulin (diabetes metabolic variables); for DM this folds definition-adjacent variables into the index.

feature_selection_quote: we ultimately focused on exploring the impact of seven routine detection indicators-age, TG, FBG, BMI, HDL-c, LDL-c, and insulin... Building on this understanding and incorporating insights from univariate regression analysis, the GLM7 formula was refined
feature_selection_note: Univariate AUC ranking of all 49 indicators was computed on the full dataset; the 7-factor GLM7 was then refined from that ranking BEFORE the train/test split -> selection used the whole sample.

reported_metrics.too_good_signature: GLM7 DM-AUC = 0.966 is the highest of the five outcomes, and HbA1c ALONE reaches 0.881 for DM -- the fingerprint of definition leakage, not a transportable signal.
